steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: This ghastly place looks scary enough on the outside, but it turns out to be even scarier on the inside! And it's so dark! I can't even see the way in front of me!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: By the way, dozens of people have died here... (Shivers) No wonder I feel a chill down my spine.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Oh Amitabha, blessed Buddha, please have mercy on us. Ladies and gents, we're just passing by. We don't want to disturb you. Just pretend that we don't exist, and keep sleeping and wandering and chatting as you would... As long as you don't bump into us.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: In short, let's just mind our own business. Please don't pick on us. After we leave, we'll make sure to burn some extra joss money and play a few extra songs for y'all. I'm a professional at this, satisfaction guaranteed...
Dudu's mouth hasn't stopped blabbering for a moment since entering the building. You know it's because she's nervous.
She's a bit short on breath, and you suddenly remember from her file that she's claustrophobic. You decide to speak up and distract her by chatting.

options: The things you just said are quite interesting.

choices.text: The things you just said are quite interesting.

steps.content: Where did you learn it from?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: ...Hmm? Oh, that. I learned it from my teacher. All my skills, including my sharp tongue, come from his teachings.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: There's no one in this world who's more interesting and remarkable than him. Without him, I really don't know what I'd be like now.
Dudu calms down a lot at the mention of her teacher. You can even detect a hint of a smile and nostalgia in her voice.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Boss, you know that I'm from the Outland. The place where I was born had long been cut off from various supplies. In order to survive, my teacher took me to DisCity.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Along the way, we cobbled together a theatrical troupe with other drifters, and made a living by forcing passers-by to watch us perform.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Those wandering days were really hard. We had nowhere to go at night, and often had to sleep in graveyards. But I was little, and staying in those places made me think of all the ghost stories I had heard about. I was so scared that I'd shake all over and not sleep a wink.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: But my teacher told me that death is not the end. It's simply a process that everyone must go through. So ghosts, graveyards, and corpses are nothing to be scared of. To help me overcome my fear, he taught me the tune I always play.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: He said it's the Song of the Phoenix. The phoenix is a symbol of reincarnation, representing both life and death. Hence, it can be played for the living as well as the dead.
Dudu's vivid description makes you visualize the scene of her as a child, hugging her knees and trembling in fear. You can't help but want to tease her again.
So you were scared of ghosts when you were a child, but not anymore?
Dudu laughs.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Not anymore.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: You know, boss? In all the years we've traveled, we've met all sorts of people.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: People who don't dare take responsibility for the sins they've committed, and beg the gods for forgiveness instead; people who pretend to be messiahs, and deceive others in the name of the gods; people who only have their own interests in mind, and don't treat others as human beings...

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: People are the only ones who harm other people. They are way scarier than any ghosts.
Her tone is light and brisk as she says this, but as the listener, you can't help but feel heavy.
What about your teacher? How is he?
You hear Dudu halt her footsteps in the darkness. She stays silent for a while before speaking again.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: He died.
What...

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: DisCity was not the city of hope that my teacher had envisioned. We came here after so much tribulation, only to run into Syndicate's most turbulent times. Once, during a gang war, someone used a mania weapon.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Everyone got infected except me. I was spared only because my teacher hid me in the cellar. But in that dark cellar, I could still hear... all the terrible noises outside.
That horrible experience might be the source of her claustrophobia.
I'm sorry. I shouldn't have brought up those bad memories...

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: ...It's fine. They're all in the past.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I buried them and played them that tune. They must have all gone to a better place, and our shared memories will forever remain in my heart.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: So I'm... not sad. I just miss them a bit every once in a while.
The dark clouds outside the window dissipate, revealing the moon. The pale moonlight shines into the dark corridor, and also upon your faces and shoulders.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: ...But I've never told anyone about these things. You're not allowed to laugh at me or tell anyone else!
Dudu sniffles and looks at you with some embarrassment. You suddenly realize that the little girl in front of you might be much tougher than you thought.
You smile at her reassuringly.
Don't worry. It'll be our little secret.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Then it's a deal! As the great MBCC Chief, you're not allowed to break your promise! Now that the moon is out and we can see the way clearly, let's move forward quickly...
Dudu's liveliness has returned to her, but after only two steps, she gasps as if she's found something, and squats down to stare at the floor.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Boss! Come see this, quick!

You go over quickly and look in the direction of her finger. You see a few faint clusters of scattered footprints amidst the gravel on the ground. Judging from the amount of dust covering them, they should be from two or three months ago.
Dudu compares her own foot with the footprints on the ground.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: It's around the same size as my foot, so it should be a woman?
The left foot makes slightly deeper prints than the right foot. This is someone with a leg injury or disability. Let's follow the footprints.
You follow the footprints to a room deep in the abandoned building.
Plastered on the charred walls are a few cartoon and sports posters. Though faded and old, there are no burn marks on them. They must have been placed there after the lightning incident.

This tells you that someone cleaned and redecorated the room after the building was abandoned. The same conclusion can be drawn from the dusty but debris-free floor and neatly arranged items on the table.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Boss! Come look at this!

Dudu takes down a framed picture from the shelf, which depicts two people. The side with the little boy is peppered with scratch marks, as if it had been repeatedly rubbed by someone's fingers. The old woman beside the boy looks familiar to you.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: That's right, it's the granny that lives next door to me!
Who's the boy? I thought she didn't have any family?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I don't know either...
Let's look separately for some more clues.
In an inconspicuous corner next to the poster is a half-burned crayon drawing. The paper is charred, so you can only make out some messy lines.
Dudu comes over.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: What is this a drawing of? What are those circles and triangles? It's so burnt that I can't tell...
You squint hard at the picture for a while.
Isn't that a square under the triangle? It looks like... a roof?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Are you sure? That's way too abstract... Huh? There seem to be words underneath?
As Dudu says this, she takes the drawing off the wall, dusts it off and wipes it with the hem of her shirt. She walks to the window and reads the words under the moonlight.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Granny and me</color>...?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: So these two circles are the heads of stick people, and the triangle is indeed a roof.
Lying quietly in the drawer is a stack of charred paper fragments, which someone had clearly rescued from the debris piece by piece and carefully preserved.
Luvia
Greeting card, New Year, eight years old, birthday, nine years old, wish you happiness, ten years old... For <color=#fb9259>Palama</color>!
After quickly sorting out all the clues from this room in your head, everything seems to click in the blink of an eye. Dudu also flashes a shocked expression upon hearing the name "Palama."

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: So... this is the house where the old lady used to live? The Palama she speaks of... is actually her grandson?!
You nod slightly.
Yet these greeting card fragments mention nothing beyond the age of ten. Something must have happened to her grandson when he was ten years old.
Those who came to explore must've seen the old lady when she was tidying the room or mourning her grandson and thought she was a ghost. This is the truth behind the haunted building.
In the end, the sharp-eyed Dudu discovers a dilapidated notebook between the table and the bed.
It's rude to look through others' personal belongings without their consent, but you can't think that much under the circumstances.
You nervously flip open the cracked cover. Written with colored pencils on the inner front page are the words "Palama's Diary."
The last piece of the puzzle has finally fallen into place. The truth of everything is within hand's reach. Your heart is racing, as if about to pop out of your throat.
The handwriting inside the diary is as childish as that of the title page, yet each pencil stroke is neat and tidy...

"Today, I went climbing a tree again. The old elm tree by the vegetable market is my favorite, but I only stayed on it for a little while before Grandma called me down. I know she worries about me, but her sudden shout is the biggest danger of all! I almost slipped and fell off..."

"Today, I fell by accident when getting eggs from the chicken coop. The pants that Grandma washed for me yesterday got dirty again. Sigh. It's hard for her to squat with her bad knees, so I thought I could help. But I ended up making her angry again."

Today is Grandma's birthday. Aside from exchanging cards as usual, I also tried making my favorite bean cake for her. Though it turned out ugly, and I put too much sugar, Grandma ate it all and said it was yummy.

"Grandma got a lot more white hair recently. I really hope she doesn't have to work so hard. Sigh, why am I only ten years old? Time passes by too slowly. I want to grow up faster so that Grandma can depend on me."
Then, there are several blank pages in a row. You continue to flip onwards.
Text reappears, but in completely different handwriting.
Palama, everyone says that you died in that accident, but I don't believe it. As long as I keep waiting, you'll come back one day, right?

"I had another big fight with the vegetable seller today. I bought so many vegetables from her, yet she refuses to give me a discount on the green onions. But I know you'd pull me away if you were there. You hate it when I fight with people. My brashness embarrasses you."

"Actually, I hate it too, but I have to force myself to be like that. If I don't try hard to be stronger, who'd protect us? Who'd protect you? I always think of your parents' accident. If I had been braver and tougher back then, would everything be different?"
"Palama, Grandma's sick. They say I have a tumor in my head that's affecting my memory. No wonder I've been having trouble finding my keys lately."
From that page onwards, the paper is frequently wrinkled from wet stains that have dried, and there are many smudged ink spots. You can almost smell the salty scent of tears.
"They say that as the tumor grows, not only will I forget my loved ones one by one, but I might also lose the ability to wash, cook, walk, and talk..."
"The other things don't matter to me. I don't care if I become a bedridden cripple, but I don't want to forget you. If I forget you, then I really have nothing."
"Grandma is really scared. What if I don't recognize you when you come back?"
"I've never done anything evil in my life, so why is fate so cruel to me? No... I won't let the last bit of hope and happiness in my life be taken away!"
After that, the handwriting becomes messier and messier, making most of the content unreadable.
You flip page after page all the way to the end. On the very last page is a final sentence, written so forcefully that it pierced through the paper...
"Palama, Grandma wants to see you one last time."
The last entry in the diary dates to three months ago. Has she already forgotten how to come to this place by now?
You gently close the diary, but your heart is still racing. In just a few minutes, you've read through her entire tragic life story from this old diary.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Chief... Let's visit the old lady and give her back the photo and diary she left behind.
Dudu's voice is a bit hoarse. She takes the framed photo from the table and gently wipes the dust off the glass.
Your heart feels just as somber as you caress the cracks on the diary cover.
Okay.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Granny? Are you there?
Dudu knocks on the door, but there's no response from inside. She twists the doorknob, and the door opens with a click.
You push open the unlocked door and walk inside, only to find that under the moonlight, the old lady had stopped breathing in her dreams.

She lies on her bed in silence, her hands folded across her stomach, her face as peaceful as a sleeping child's. The clear moonlight cascading in from the window bathes her in an almost sacred silver sheen.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Granny, this is the first time that I've seen such a kind and gentle smile on your glum face...

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: You must've reached another world by now, reunited with your family and that precious grandson you've been waiting decades for, right?
Yeah. She's been losing things her entire life. She lost her family, her grandson, her health, and even her memory, but she never lost hope.
You solemnly put the photo and diary back into the old lady's arms. The lost treasures have finally been returned to their rightful owner.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Now... It's time for me to deliver on my promise.

Dudu stands by the window and starts to play her song. Under the moonlight, the suona's blaring wails sound mournfully beautiful, as if each note drifting into the night breeze carries a memory of the old lady and her grandson.

The hard but happy life they shared seems to unfold before your eyes. You see the undying resilience that kept the old lady going in the lonely days after the incident. You hear her call out to her grandson again and again as she reminisces his smiling face, if only to remember his name...
And when all the dust has settled, you see the most beautiful reunion that belongs to her dreams.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Chief...
When the song is finished, Dudu puts down the suona and looks up at you, her eyes filled with sorrow.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: My teacher told me before that death is not the ultimate end of a life, but being forgotten is.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Now that Granny is gone, will Palama completely disappear from this world?
You take a deep breath and look at Dudu with warm, reassuring eyes.
At least we shall remember him for her.
